claims.statement: JSON Schema is the canonical contract system at trust boundaries, AJV validates those boundaries, and generated contract declarations are produced from an explicit registry by `scripts/generate-foundation-contract.mjs`.
The package-level verification commands distinguish contract generation, type checks, frontend validation/build/tests, backend tests, and a chained `npm run check` command that runs all of them.

Project test policy directs developers to start with relevant static checks and the smallest meaningful behavior test, expand coverage for changed boundaries or risk, and use synthetic fixtures rather than real runtime data; external provider calls require task-specific authorization.

Report-version requests enforce an ordered semantic history: version 1 has no predecessor while later versions require a SHA-256 predecessor; persisted report records bind request, workspace/source/evidence/semantic/review digests and retained artifact metadata.

`ReportVersionService` validates snapshots before creation, serializes creation through a database mutation mutex, persists artifact references and version metadata in a transaction, and rereads the version to verify the returned identity.
Exact report-version retries are deduplicated with zero database mutations; tests require recovery of a missing exact publication but reject corruption rather than replacing corrupted bytes.

Prepared report creation binds retained preparation, readiness, section, catalog, package, and source lineage, rejects drift before persistence, and preserves historical artifacts when appending a new profile.

Historical Metric-method verification is designed to replay frozen retained bytes without reading a live workspace, clock, Python/calculator path, or writing to the database; retained-byte corruption is an integrity failure.

Research-automation revisions are contractually anchored to a prior report-pair digest and are exposed as asynchronous attempt receipts whose states include queued, running, committed, failed, and cancelled.

`ResearchAutomationService` leaves source/provider and AI transports optional by constructor injection, and source-keyword drafting reports `MODEL_NOT_CONFIGURED` rather than invoking a model when no transport is supplied.

The automation draft-revision integration test uses a temporary database, artifact store, fixed clock/UUID, fixture collector, and in-process renderer, and verifies exact retry has no writes while invalid requests retain no evidence.

Provider collection configuration fails closed: review collection needs both a token and explicit bounded charge cap, TikTok comment configuration is absent by default, and malformed caps are rejected without exposing tokens.

The PageIndex integration path uses fake HTTP while exercising real service attachment, local quote verification, persistence, and artifacts; it verifies SHA-based upload deduplication, caps, low-balance/usage-limit dispatch prevention, and no provider call on read-only page loads.

Frontend tests use jsdom and fake fetch to verify that unknown AI billing is not displayed as zero and retained report-history reloads are GET-only, preserve explicit version selection, and disable revision writes when history is incomplete or has an integrity error.
The documented research batch identifies `d9bd883` as its `origin/main` base and requires no real provider or AI call in tests plus byte-identical stored report-version readback.

The contract generator compiles an explicit registry of JSON Schemas into adjacent generated TypeScript declarations and marks those outputs as not hand-editable; it does not itself run validation checks.

Report version creation accepts a closed schema-defined request whose first version has no predecessor and whose later versions require a digest predecessor; persisted records retain identity, source and artifact digests, selected sources, and initial unreviewed states.

ReportVersionService serializes report creation under a database mutation mutex, persists content-addressed artifacts and version metadata transactionally, then reopens the version to verify the returned receipt identity.

A report-version read verifies canonical request identity, every registered artifact and exact rebuilt file set, lineage and selected-source membership, then validates the record projection before returning it.

An exact report-version retry is mutation-free and can restore a missing artifact only after rebuilding and verifying it; corrupted retained bytes remain an integrity failure rather than being replaced.

Report presentation can yield distinct retained HTML while preserving semantic identity, and the integration tests assert that legacy report artifacts remain unchanged across that presentation evolution.

ResearchAutomationService accepts a revision only after validating and canonicalizing its request, verifying the current predecessor and selected sources, and retaining a QUEUED attempt; request-key retries are idempotent while stale predecessors and concurrent active attempts conflict.

Automation version and attempt reads verify the committed predecessor chain and attempt sequence, reject inconsistent state, and support explicitly selected report pairs rather than treating a historical pair as current.
Metric historical verification is tested with live workspace, clock, Python execution, and database writes unavailable, and it rejects altered snapshot or retained artifact bytes.
Provider configuration tests require explicit bounded charge configuration, keep absent configurations disabled, and verify malformed caps do not echo the supplied token.

The PageIndex integration fixture uses fake HTTP responses while exercising real service, attachment, verification, SQLite, and artifact boundaries, including upload deduplication, durable question caps, spend gating, and read-only status behavior.

Frontend tests use jsdom and replaced fetch to verify unknown billing display, immutable multipart source requests, read-only history reload, explicit pair selection, integrity gating, and retry request identity.
